title: One camera for exploring and building
changes: Opening or closing the build tray keeps the same camera distance, heading and pitch. Exploration and building share one continuous wheel zoom, with a wider default view and room to pull back.

Enclosed rooms keep their own closer framing in both gameplay and building. Open shelters do not force a close-up. Real walls and ceilings can shorten the camera arm further; leaving the room smoothly restores your outdoor zoom.

Camera clearance follows nearby building surfaces, including real door openings and gaps between beams. A small camera volume prevents its edges from passing through walls; a wider lens helps when space is tight. Brief gaps between obstacles do not pump the zoom, and the avatar clears the view when a wall forces the camera very close.

Normal perspective building keeps walls and roofs solid. Manual ghost/hidden storeys remain available, and the optional isometric view retains its cutaway. Camera changes do not alter structural collision, support or saved buildings.

title: General timber frames and joined roof slopes
changes: General wood beams, metal-bound beams and narrow planks can be posts, horizontal members, rafters or shelves. Choose 1 / 2 / 4 m, adjust with Q/E, or use FIT between two joints for the exact length. Material cost follows length.

End sockets and side sockets at every metre work on either part. Z / Shift+Z chooses the carried station and nearby target face. R / Shift+R turns the part, Shift+C changes pitch in 22.5-degree steps, and the selected joint stays fixed.

Wood carries 4 m laterally from a grounded bearing; metal-bound timber carries 8 m and planks 2 m. Opposing bearings share a span. Short pieces, floating loops and a post above a weak cantilever cannot reset this budget. Existing material-height, fire and collapse rules still apply.
Cover boards fit between parallel general timbers up to 2 m apart. New frames carry snow without reciprocal joints disabling the snow-load graph. Intact recovered timbers keep their original length.

Quick roof tiles have an optional JOIN setting with HIP and VALLEY modes. Real crossing slopes are cut on both sides at arbitrary angles; picking, walking, snow, support and smoke use the cut faces. Removing a neighbour restores the original outline, including after save/load and undo.
Existing specialist roof parts, buildings and saves remain compatible. Frame picking and bearing checks stay local; unchanged previews reuse their last evaluation.

title: Wider steps and vertical stacking
changes: Aim at the left or right side centre of a modular step to join another tread at the same height and make the stair wider. Both narrow sides have four corner sockets and a centre.
Front and rear centre sockets still extend tread depth. Z / Shift+Z also selects top and bottom centre sockets for vertical stacking; ordinary ascending stairs remain the default.
Side and stacked joins use physical contact for support, save/load, fire and collapse. A corner touch or a floating cycle cannot support the widened stair.

title: Open hearths and fires made from loose fuel
changes: The Camp build tray includes an open 1 × 2 m stone hearth. It starts empty and can stand on a supported floor or level ground.
Face the hearth and use DROP 1 in the backpack to add branches, logs or charcoal. Fuel stays cold until a flame reaches it; tinder and flint remain available through the camp interactions.
Dropped branches and logs can now become a campfire when touched by a flame, Burning water or a Fire Gate rune. Nearby dropped fuel joins the fire and burns only once.
Fuel, heat, smoke and remaining burn time use the existing camp simulation and persist with your world. Flames respect walls and storey height; covered braziers cannot ignite loose fuel.
Spent logs and groups of branches leave collectible charcoal after the embers cool. Charcoal gives a longer, quieter burn and cannot produce more charcoal.

title: Stair end sockets and reliable wall placement
changes: Modular steps have five sockets at each end: four corners and a centre. Nearby step joins take priority over walls and floors. Centre joins extend a tread at the same height; corner joins continue the rise.
Press Z for the next valid socket placement, or Shift+Z for the previous one. A selected attachment stays selected while aiming at the same spot. The build toolbar also has a socket button.
Upper floors prefer the player side at stacked wall seams. Floor rotations use the wall centreline, and narrow deck seams are easier to target from below.

Window walls inherit the exact angle of the wall they replace in both Socket and Grid modes, including walls rotated independently of their building grid. Wider 45-degree bays receive a matching wide window.
New stair joins retain physical support, save/load and collapse behaviour; an isolated corner touch cannot support a floating step.

title: Modular steps and updates that keep your world
changes: Build stairs one step at a time from floors, wall faces or another step. Five standard steps climb half a storey; ten climb a full storey. Turned steps share an exact connecting edge.
Use G for a local surface grid, R / Shift+R to turn, C to reverse, and Q/E to adjust the step length. Steps participate in structural support, fire, collapse and saves.
Upper floors and roof tiles placed on a wall prefer the player’s side. Pointing near a wall’s upper edge from below also selects the upper-floor bearing.
An update notice lets you save and restart into the newest build. Your buildings, inventory and world progress are preserved. Full reset remains a separate option in the top bar.
Open the version button in the top bar to read the patch history. This is the first entry in the in-game archive; earlier development reports remain in the project documentation.
